<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for `designcraft-git`, a Git-based AUR package. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is appropriate here because the source is a Git repository (VCS), and checksums are not applicable — this is a common and accepted practice for `-git` packages.

The build process uses standard Cargo commands (`cargo fetch`, `cargo build`) with environment variables configured to control build behavior, such as enabling debug info and disabling LTO stripping. These are reasonable settings for a development-focused package. All installed files are built locally from the source and placed in standard system locations: binaries in `/usr/bin`, desktop files in `/usr/share/applications`, MIME info in `/usr/share/mime`, icons in `/usr/share/icons`, and licenses in `/usr/share/licenses`. There are no network requests, downloads, or executions from external sources during the build or install phases.

No obfuscated code, suspicious scripts, or unexpected system modifications are present. The package conflicts with the non-git version of the same software and provides a virtual package, which is normal packaging practice. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging workflows and upstream Rust/cargo conventions.
</details>
